node.title: Generating SVG Badges with Perl
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
If you've looked at projects on GitHub or other sites, you may have noticed the little rectangular badges (aka shields) saying things like "build passing" with a nice green background (or yellow/red if something is wrong), and if you've used [https://travis-ci.org/|Travis CI] or [https://coveralls.io/|Coveralls], you probably know how to get these badges. There is also a nice service that can generate these badges for you, [https://shields.io/|Shields.io], which is [https://github.com/badges/shields|written] in JavaScript.

There didn't seem to be anything like that for Perl, so I wrote [mod://Badge::Simple]!

Thanks to a super quick turnaround by [https://github.com/charsbar|Kenichi Ishigaki], these badges are already integrated into [https://cpants.cpanauthors.org/|CPANTS]: Try accessing https://cpants.cpanauthors.org/dist/Your-Dist-Name.svg or https://cpants.cpanauthors.org/author/YOURCPANID.svg and you should see a badge for your Kwalitee score (PNG badges have also been [https://github.com/cpants/www-cpants/issues/69|available] for quite some time, just use .png instead of .svg).

In the respository, you can find the script [https://github.com/haukex/Badge-Simple/blob/master/misc/cpantesters.pl|cpantesters.pl], which you can use to generate CPAN Testers badges for your CPAN modules. There is an [https://github.com/cpan-testers/cpantesters-web/issues/20|open issue] to perhaps integrate this directly with CPAN Testers, if anyone would like to take a stab at that, please feel free :-)

You can see all this in action, for example, in the [https://github.com/haukex/Badge-Simple/blob/master/README.md#badge-simple|Badge-Simple readme]: the "Kwalitee" and "CPAN Testers" badges were generated with Perl!
